newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom up on placement, other Russian shares quiet.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom up on placement, other Russian shares quiet.

text.p: Shares in Gazprom jumped on Friday on news the gas monopoly would shortly make an international placement of depositary receipts, but other leading Russian shares were barely changed in quiet trade.
Dealers said Gazprom, which by early afternoon was up over six percent, could end the day with strong gains.
At 1015 GMT it was traded at $0.345 after Thursday's closing $0.325.
Although Gazprom is Russia's biggest company by market capitalisation, its shares are highly illiquid because of company restrictions on buying and selling them.
"Receipts are a positive factor since to re-register Gazprom shares is a complicated affair," said Ilya Sapozhnikov of Credit Suisse Moskva.
"Gazprom in itself is a very strong and attractive company. In general, when a leading company issues depository receipts it is likely to move the market," he said.
A source close to the deal said Gazprom would place depository receipts in early October on the London Stock Exchange or through a consortium of international investment banks.
Andrei Ippolitov of Prospect said the overall market could advance today on the Gazprom news, but only slightly.
"Gazprom is trying to move the market upwards, but... buyers are not aggressive. This week, in general, there were buyers but they were not ready to pay high prices," he said.
LUKoil rose to $9.54 from Thursday's close at $9.50. UES was unchanged at $0.0770. Norilsk Nickel edged down to $6.66 from $6.71, and Mosenergo eased to $0.943 from $0.948.
